display.title: Episode 165: Three Lost on an Island, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: In Adar, Uncle Yossi teaches Ki Karov Eilecha, a listener tells of Rabbi Tarfon honoring his mother, and the island story ends with a lesson about the neshamah.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens in the happy month of Adar and teaches number five of the Twelve Pesukim, Ki Karov Eilecha: serving Hashem with our mouth, heart and actions is very close to us; we try our best and Hashem does the rest. The Hakochainik march sings it, and listeners hear about a new Torah trivia club with points and prizes. In Mitzvah Time a girl reads her composition about how Rabbi Tarfon honored his sick mother. After a recap and the Shema with a ten-year-old yeshiva student, 'Three Lost on an Island' concludes. Through the telescope the survivors see a castle with a notice that the queen is ill. They fly there, the doctor's apple cures her, and each man claims the reward of marrying the princess. The king rewards all three with treasure but gives his daughter to the doctor, whose apple is the one thing he could not get elsewhere. Uncle Yossi explains the mashal: our possessions, our body and our neshamah all matter, but only the neshamah, with its Torah and mitzvos, goes on to the world to come. The show ends with a grager and a promise of Purim visitors next week.
display.lesson: Food, clothing, shelter and the body are all needed, but the neshamah is what lasts forever; only Torah and good deeds go with a person to the world to come.

date.note: Week after ep. 164 (19 Feb 1985, eve of Rosh Chodesh Adar); 'here we are in the month of Adar' and the Purim program is 'next week'. Weekly estimate was 3 weeks late.

advisories.note: A queen is gravely ill until the doctor's apple cures her; a listener's composition mentions Rabbi Tarfon's sick mother.

sources_cited.note: Not silver, gold or jewels accompany a person, only Torah and good deeds.
Hashem, Yisroel and the Torah are one and eternal.
